title: Rare 4K footage of the barreleye fish with a transparent head (MBARI)
verification: Read the MBARI-based ScienceDaily article of Nov 17, 2026: depth, distance, vessel, ROV, 11 encounters in ~4 decades and ~7,000 dives, eye behavior, diet. Single institutional source (MBARI first-hand observation); no journal paper.

It took 7,000 dives and more than 41,000 hours of video to get 11 meetings.

caption:
Imagine eyes that sit inside your head, under a clear dome.

That is the barreleye fish, Macropinna microstoma. Researchers at the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) spotted one about 1,970 feet (600 m) down, roughly 55 miles (90 km) offshore in the Pacific, and filmed it for about 20 minutes. It was reported on November 17, 2026.

The fish has tube-shaped eyes that normally point up, to catch the silhouettes of animals passing overhead. When it spots prey, the eyes rotate forward inside a transparent, jelly-like dome on top of its head. Big fins let it hover almost motionless.

It eats small crustaceans caught in the stinging tentacles of siphonophores, and the dome protects its eyes while it does.

This was only MBARI's 11th encounter in nearly four decades. Those meetings came out of about 7,000 dives and more than 41,000 hours of deep-sea video. The last one was in 2021. It was also the first 4K footage of the species, and the first from the research vessel David Packard.

Senior scientist Steven Haddock called seeing it a rare treat.

Source: MBARI via ScienceDaily
variety_exception: Both stories were found through ScienceDaily but come from different institutions (Columbia University and MBARI) and are far apart in subject.
